transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?
I came in because I can’t make myself go near the front windows or that part of the street anymore. I keep finding excuses to stay in the back, even though being out front is part of my job.
Can you tell me what it is about being near the front windows or that part of the street that worries you—did something happen there?

Something happened around there, and now I just can’t make myself go near the front windows or that part of the street. I keep finding reasons to stay in the back, even though working out front is part of my job.
Can you describe exactly what happened that day near the front windows or that part of the street?
I’m sorry, I don’t really know how to describe it. I just know that area feels impossible for me to be around now.
How long ago did this event near the front windows happen?
About two weeks ago. It was during an overnight shift—the car crashed through the store window.
Since that night, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about the crash that intrude on your mind even when you don't want them to?
Yeah. It just pops into my head out of nowhere, especially when I’m setting up displays. Suddenly I can hear that bang and see the glass coming down, like it’s happening again.
Did these intrusive memories and flashbacks start right after the crash, and have you been experiencing them nearly every day since then, or did they come and go at first?
It started after the crash. Since then it keeps coming into my head out of nowhere, especially when I’m setting up displays—I hear the bang and see the glass falling like it’s happening again.
Since the crash, have you noticed yourself feeling unusually jumpy or on edge, startling easily at sudden noises, or feeling like you always need to be on guard?
Yeah. If a delivery cart bangs or a car honks outside, I jump really hard—my whole body jerks. Even if someone comes up behind me, it gets me, and then my heart keeps racing afterward.
Since the crash, have you noticed yourself feeling emotionally numb, detached from what's happening around you, or like things feel unreal or dreamlike?
Sometimes on the sales floor, everything feels kind of far away and fake—the lights, the racks. It’s like I’m watching myself move through the store instead of really being there.
Since the crash, have you noticed a persistent low or negative mood, or found it hard to feel happiness, love, or other positive emotions that you used to feel easily?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a big change in that, honestly.
Besides staying away from the front windows, have you been avoiding other reminders of the crash—like talking about it, thinking about it, or certain sounds or situations that remind you of it?
Yeah. I keep making excuses to stay in the back instead of going near the front windows or that part of the street. It’s part of my job, but I just... can’t make myself go over there.
Since the crash two weeks ago, have these symptoms—like the flashbacks, jumpiness, and avoidance—been continuing steadily every day, or have you noticed them starting to ease up at all?
It’s been pretty steady. Ever since the car crashed through the store window during that overnight shift, so about two weeks now.
